messages:
maria: quick thought — the current single query surface is making it hard to meet steady-state p50 SLOs when tenant workloads mix live dashboards + heavy batch exports.
aj: yup been noticing p50 jumps during report windows. is this the same fanout hotspot we saw last week?
jia: looks related. the fanout path for 'render' pulls a ton of historical tiles and we do auth checks per tile which multiplies latency.
maria: proposal: split the console surface into two explicit surfaces — a fast-path for live interactive panels (strict latency budget, coarse auth checks) and a materialize-path for heavy, consistency-focused fanouts (async, stronger correctness).
tyler: hmm. coarse auth checks for fast-path = pushdown of role->capability token at route level rather than per-tile? that reduces per-item auth rpc.
aj: tradeoff: weaker auth granularity on fast-path could leak stale perms if we cache tokens too long. need TTL heuristics.
jia: we can bound exposure: fast-path only surfaces tenant-scoped views (no cross-tenant join), and ACLs that change frequently can bypass cache.
maria: also thinking: fast-path should prefer prefix/KV cache and avoid rehydrating heavy materializers. materialize-path can do the expensive joins and strict per-record filters.
tyler: how do we model fallback? if fast-path cache miss or mismatch, fall back to materialize-path automatically? that would keep UX intact.
aj: fallback is reasonable but must be circuit-breaker protected — otherwise heavy requests will flood materialize pool.
jia: agreed. we should add an admission-control token: fast-path downgrade only allowed for < 5% of requests per tenant per minute by default.
maria: ops-bot, can you file an RFC stub with the surface split, auth pushdown, fallback & admission rules? link it back here. :pray:
ops-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/console-surface-split-1709876543 — outline added.
tyler: perf numbers we need from runtime: p50/p95 for current mixed traffic, per-tenant auth rpc QPS, cache hit rates. QA: can infra run a 2h replay with synthetic dashboard traffic?
aj: I'll run replay against staging. will include a variation that forces 20% heavier exports to stress fanout.
jia: spike owners? I'll take auth pushdown prototyping (server side token interfaces + TTL semantics).
maria: I'll own routing policy + admission control config and the RFC writeup.
tyler: small nit: name the surfaces something obvious in code — e.g., console.fastpath and console.materialize — so telemetries don't get confusing.
tyler: also we need a migration plan: defaults stay on single surface. opt-in per-tenant flag to split. after stabilization we flip for high-traffic tenants first.
aj: operational checklist: monitoring dashboards for fallback rate, materialize queue length, auth cache eviction rate, and end-to-end p50.
jmaria: tiny correction — that's maria not jmaria :)
maria: lol thanks.
jia: timeline suggestion: 2-week spike, then small canary with 2 tenants, measure 7 days, iterate.
aj: ack. starting replay now, will post numbers by tomorrow EOD.
tyler: one more thought on RBAC semantics: materialize-path should enforce policy filters server-side not just rely on tokens; that's safer for compliance customers.
maria: yep materialize enforces full predicate pushdown. fast-path gives a token that encodes tenant+role+expiry and the renderer enforces coarse post-filtering.
aj: leaving an example token shape here:
```
{
  "tenant": "t-abc123",
  "role": "viewer",
  "scope": "panel:read",
  "exp": 1709962943,
  "flags": ["no-cross-join"]
}
```
jia: action items: aj: run replays + post perf; jia: auth spike PR; maria: RFC + routing policy; tyler: telemetry alert defs + canary plan.
maria: agreed. sync tomorrow 10am to decide go/no-go for canary. :calendar:
aj: dropping logs in thread in a bit.
ops-bot: Reminder: sync scheduled for 10:00 tomorrow in #eng-platform.
